checks.evidence: Action: Observe the rendered sun/three differently sized blue, gold and purple planets, automatic motion, and seek 0,6,12,24,48 seconds while reading each selected angle and measuring transient screenshot color components. Expected: Circular fixed-phase 12/24/48-second orbits. Observed: Initial angles were 20.05/120.32/260.70 degrees; at 6 seconds 200.05/210.32/305.70. Aurora returned to its identical rendered component at 12 seconds, Ceres at 24, and all three at 48. Loaded source uses radii 4.4/6.8/9.3 and fixed phases .35/2.1/4.55 radians; observed positions and motion agree with those periods, not merely constants.

Action: Open fresh scene and reload in the same origin after imports/captures. Expected: Time zero initialization, 1x, running, no selection, overview followed by motion. Observed: Reload readouts began at 0.04, 0.05 and 0.08 seconds after load with Pause, 1.00x, explicit no-selection information and disabled tracking; no snapshot auto-restored. Initial uninterrupted visible 1x sample advanced 5.21 to 8.32 seconds in 3.1037 wall seconds.

Action: Pause during tracking, seek 17 and 30, wait at least three seconds, select and orbit while paused, then resume. Expected: Frozen time and orbital positions with usable selection/camera and no resume jump. Observed: Paused 17.00 remained exact through waits at all tested speeds; screenshot planet components were identical before/after 3.1-second waits. Selection and camera drag/zoom worked while paused. Resume began from sought state and measured deltas matched the active speed.

Action: Change 0.25x, 2x and 4x both paused and playing; resume each paused change and measure uninterrupted visible page-clock/time pairs over at least 3.1 seconds. Expected: Current time/positions preserved and common orbital rate changes. Observed: Paused 17.00 and all rendered components stayed identical at every speed. Resume samples were 0.76/3.1029, 6.21/3.1029 and 12.38/3.1033 simulation/wall seconds; playing-change samples were 0.78/3.1031, 6.22/3.1024 and 12.37/3.1015. All meet preregistered tolerances; no reset/jump, and planet information remains consistent with the same fixed-period time formula.

Action: Use real seek range for 0,30,120,17,73; revisit 30,17,73 after speed/playback/selection changes and after reload; restore fractional 17.25 through valid JSON. Expected: Seeking pauses and immediately synchronizes time/positions/info/tracking with fixed phases. Observed: All integer seeks showed exact requested time and Resume. At 30 angles were 200.05/210.32/125.70, at 17 170.05/15.32/28.20, at 73 50.05/135.32/88.20. Three planets’ rendered color-component centroids repeated exactly in aligned 353x369 scene images before/after reload; fractional restore showed 177.6/19.1/30.1 degrees. Tracking remained centered immediately at seeks.

Action: Seek 119, set 4x, resume across endpoint, wait again, seek 17 and resume. Expected: Stop at 120 without wrap/overshoot and restart earlier. Observed: Both endpoint reads were 120.00 with Resume; later seek/resume advanced 17.91 to 30.28 in 3.1028 wall seconds at 4x.

Action: Inspect loaded CDN/renderer implementation and orbit/zoom rendered scene in overview/tracking, paused/playing. Expected: Genuine Three.js 3D geometry and perspective. Observed: HTTP resource timing identified Three.js 0.160.1; index.html lines 53-57 instantiate WebGLRenderer, PerspectiveCamera, SphereGeometry and 3D circular orbits. Rendered spherical shading, foreground/background overlap, orbit-plane tilt and relative positions changed under native drags; zoom changed apparent body size. This is rendered depth evidence, not an import-only inference.

Action: Capture paused A at 30/2x/Dione/tracking, edit every live field and resume, restore; capture while running, export/import/reload, and restore imported 17.25 with bogus supplied angles. Expected: Immutable captured fields/all angles, unique stable IDs, no live mutation and time-derived angles. Observed: A obs-mvgq3hiu-1 retained 30.00/2.00x/Dione/tracking and 200.1/210.3/125.7 degrees through edits. Playing capture retained 0.11/1x/null/overview and its derived angles across reload. Captured three-entry JSON exported, reimported, reloaded and exported byte-identically. Fractional imported 17.25 displayed 177.6/19.1/30.1, ignoring supplied 999-degree angles. All five saved fields, ID and three angles are visible in each row.

Action: Native canvas-click and labeled-list select Aurora, Ceres and Dione separately while paused and while playing. Expected: Both routes synchronize selection, highlight and information. Observed: Six canvas trials at time 0 or approximately 0.06 seconds selected the intended planet, then list-switch-away/back selected it again. Paused trials retained Resume; playing trials retained Pause. Buttons and brightened/enlarged rendered bodies shared selection; individual info showed the correct stable ID and 12/24/48-second period.

Action: Inspect each selected planet during playback and seeking, startup no selection and null-snapshot restore. Expected: Accurate live name/period/angle and explicit cleared no-selection state. Observed: Selected readouts matched fixed-phase rendered positions and updated continuously; e.g. Dione 125.70 at 30 and 88.20 at 73. Null restore cleared all pressed planet buttons/highlight and showed No planet selected, not stale planet information.

Action: Track all three while playing, switch targets, seek paused 30/73 and inspect disabled tracking with no selection. Expected: Centered selected body and synchronized target/info/highlight without resetting state. Observed: Native rendered-image samples spanning over 3 seconds per planet stayed within 13 CSS pixels of scene center (186.67,184.40), below 35.31-pixel tolerance; Ceres samples were about (186.20,183.84) and (186.36,183.86). Dione remained centered at immediate seeks. List switches retained 1x and running playback with only natural time advance. Null startup/restores disabled tracking.

Action: At 390x844 select Dione, track, pause/seek 30, and activate Full-system overview; also return from each playing tracking target. Expected: Entire system visible while preserving selection/time/speed/playback. Observed: State preservation worked, but the standard overview at 30 clipped Dione against the canvas left boundary; its body and outer orbit extended outside the rendered scene. This is canvas clipping, not vertical page scrolling. Source index.html line 47 fixes overview distance at 23 and line 60 changes aspect without fitting horizontal extent.

Action: Restore selected tracking and null overview snapshots after time/selection/mode edits and manual orbit/zoom; repeat restores at the same viewport. Expected: Atomic paused state plus deterministic standard tracking/full-system overview framing. Observed: Exact fields, cleared information, angles and pause state restored; repeated aligned image centroids were identical for tracking and null overview. However restoring Null overview at time 30, speed 1.5 at 390x844 again clipped Dione at the left canvas edge, so the required standard full-system overview framing is not achieved. Same fixed overview-distance cause as T4.

Action: Native orbit drags and wheel zoom in overview/tracking both paused and playing. Expected: Both controls operate around current target without changing simulation state. Observed: Four mode/playback combinations changed rendered geometry view, relative planet locations and apparent size. In paused overview Ceres component moved from about (256.3,250.6) to (167.7,210.9) after orbit and (170.4,206.7) after zoom while time stayed 17.00. Paused tracking held Ceres centered while other bodies shifted and its colored area shrank from 3797 to 2240 pixels under zoom. Playing combinations retained Pause and natural advancement.

Action: Restore no-selection overview at time 0; pointer-down on Ceres, move twenty 1-CSS-pixel steps right and twenty back before pointer-up (40 pixels cumulative); compare fast 60x20 drag and DOM interactions. Expected: A camera drag never selects a planet. Observed: Slow drag changed selection from null to Ceres at unchanged 0.00, while fast drag left selection null. Source line 62 resets drag x/y every move and marks moved only when a single-event Manhattan delta exceeds 3; cumulative motion is therefore misclassified as a click. DOM button/range/snapshot/JSON operations did not leak scene selection.

Action: Inspect controls, status labels and feedback across playback, selection, tracking, capacity, snapshots and JSON operations. Expected: Understandable observation workflow. Observed: Explicit Pause/Resume, numeric speed/time, selected name/ID/period/angle, camera-mode info, captured fields, visible capacity/rejection/import/export messages and stable-ID mapping make ordinary operation clear. Coherent, usable ordinary execution (anchor 3), rather than exceptional presentation; the separately scored saving-warning defect is not an extra qualitative penalty.
